rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2, 2.6 and 3.1 - the authors train and test SVM, ANN and RVM models on their own six-year lysimeter dataset (pepper and watermelon, drip and sub-irrigation, plastic mulch) and compare predicted Kc against lysimeter-measured Kc (Tables 3-6, Figs 3-4).
rows.notes: The study reports its own result only on machine-learning prediction of crop coefficients and crop ET (SVM r2 = 0.71 pepper, 0.82 watermelon; ETc errors 2.6-11.2% vs 35-42% for FAO-56) and on scaling that error to a 112 ha farm water budget. It does not implement or test any irrigation scheduling application, nor measure irrigation efficiency, applied water or water savings. Water conservation through improved scheduling is only stated as a potential use (Introduction, Conclusions), so the study supports at most a precondition (better ETc estimates) of the claimed efficiency gain. Q3-Q9 therefore answered no.

notes: Full text available and complete. Study is a Kc/ETc prediction modelling paper using lysimeter data from south Florida; no irrigation scheduling or efficiency outcome was measured.
